title: Customer Service Advisor
description:
Summary:
Job Title: Customer Service Advisor (Call Center)
Location: Snodland, Kent, UK (In-person)
Salary: £25,948.87 + Performance based bonus + Benefits
Are you looking to join a team that shares your passion for providing excellent customer service?
Are you a determined individual? Do you enjoy a sense of achievement when hitting targets and goals?
If so, this is a chance you won't want to pass up!
We are recruiting for multiple roles for several critical positions within our fast-paced, friendly, and award-winning Customer Service team. As part of your role you will understand your customer's point of view and make them feel heard. Your warmth, passion, and commitment will assist us in getting it right the first time for our customers.
No two days are the same. Upon starting within our call centre, you'll help customers with water bills, refunds, payment plans, and occupant changes. You'll also be ready to assist if they have problems with their water supply. If you enjoy working towards targets, love problem solving, and take satisfaction in delivering the best solutions possible, then this is the role for you.
Working on a full time 37 hour week, you'll be assigned a shift pattern that includes one Saturday every six weeks. These shifts can be any time Monday through Friday, 08:00 - 19:00, and on the one Saturday, 08:00 - 13:00. The rotas are created in advance so that you are able to plan around them.
This position also offers numerous prospects for progression. For example, most of our management began their careers as Customer Service Advisors. You'll have the opportunity to move throughout the department to learn new skills and try out for other roles. As a result, now is a perfect opportunity to launch a successful career and contribute to the success of our Customer Service team.
Main responsibilities:
- Take calls from South Eastern Water Customers and assist with their requests, queries or complaints.
- Provide an excellent customer experience by being flexible to resolve all customer contacts within the company timescales and contribute to customer satisfaction score.
- Maintain focus on meeting targets and adhere to business processes, data protection, regulatory compliance and attendance.
- Build relationships with peers and colleagues to enhance the team working environment, resolve customer problems and ensure successful productivity.
- Proactively use information and resources to ensure that skills and knowledge are kept up to date and continuously developed.
- Attend and contribute to team meetings with team, peers and colleagues.
- To be available to support the business in peak periods by covering post room and reception duties and by being part of a standby rota emergency periods.

What you'll need:
Essential Skills / Qualifications / Experience
- Commitment to providing excellent customer service
- Dedication to finding the best solutions to problems
- Excellent computer abilities
- Outstanding writing and vocal communication abilities
- Ability to handle frequent phone calls via headset throughout most of your working day

Desirable Skills / Qualifications / Experience
- Previous customer service / call centre experience would be advantageous but is not essential

What to expect from our recruitment process:
- Initial CV review
- Invitation to complete online video recording of yourself answering qualifying questions
- Invitation to attend assessment day onsite with us at Snodland alongside other candidates for a morning/afternoon of group activities, collaboration, and a short final interview.

Grow a career with a meaningful purpose.
We know the communities we serve are diverse. We recognise creativity comes from diversity not similarity. That's why we are enthusiastic about creating inclusion across age, race, gender, ethnicity, religion and identity. You will experience our dedication to equal opportunities and fair treatment for all: through your recruitment, employment and career progression with South East Water.
Benefits package:
- Excellent Stakeholder pension scheme, up to 10% employer contribution.
- 5 weeks holiday plus bank holidays per annum, increasing to 6 weeks with length of service.
- Flexible annual leave policy to buy or sell holiday leave.
- Paid volunteering days.
- Cycle to work scheme.
- Health cash plan.
- Life assurance.
- Wellbeing related benefits.

What can you expect from your recruitment?
- To apply for this position, please submit your CV on our career's website.
- It is necessary for you to have the legal right to work in the UK when you begin employment with South East Water.
- Additionally, as part of the employment offer, you will need to pass background, identity, and employment referencing checks.

title: Lettings Administrator

PART-TIME LETTINGS CONTRACTS ADMINISTRATOR

STUDENT ACCOMMODATION, CANTERBURY

MONDAY - FRIDAY / 10:00 - 14:30 / 22.5 HOURS PER WEEK

SALARY £27,000 (PRO RATA'D ACCORDINGLY BASED ON 22.5 HOURS PER WEEK)

We re looking for an exceptional organiser who knows lettings contracts inside out.

Westgate One is looking for an experienced Lettings Contracts & Compliance Administrator to join our small, friendly and incredibly busy team.

This is a key role within our student accommodation operation.

You will take ownership of the administrative and compliance journey from an applicant agreeing to take a property through to their tenancy commencing, making sure that every check, document, payment and deadline is dealt with accurately and on time.

This is not an entry-level lettings position. We are looking for someone who already has practical experience of residential lettings administration/contracts in England and understands the importance of getting the detail right.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:

You'll manage the tenancy application and contracting process, including:
- Carrying out Right to Rent checks and maintaining appropriate evidence.
- Managing applicant referencing.
- Coordinating guarantor checks and guarantor agreements.
- Carrying out or coordinating affordability and credit checks.
- Completing relevant anti-money laundering and identity verification procedures in accordance with the requirements applicable to our business.
- Ensuring our tenancy processes remain compliant with the Renters' Rights Act 2025 and other relevant lettings legislation.
- Supporting Westgate One's compliance with the new Private Rented Sector Database as it is introduced.
- Preparing appropriate tenancy agreements and issuing documentation for electronic signature.
- Taking and correctly administering holding deposits.
- Issuing balance requests for first rent payments at the appropriate time.
- Registering tenancy deposits with the relevant government-authorised tenancy deposit protection scheme and ensuring required information is issued.
- Actively progressing applications rather than simply waiting for paperwork to come back.
- Regularly speaking with applicants, tenants, parents and guarantors to resolve queries and keep applications moving.
- Monitoring outstanding actions and key dates so nothing gets missed and tenancy commencement dates remain on track.
- Keeping accurate and complete tenancy, compliance and audit records.
- Handling applicants' personal and financial information sensitively and in accordance with UK GDPR and data protection requirements.

You'll also be part of a small operational team, so from time to time you'll get involved in wider tasks such as:
- Property and room inspections
- Meter readings
- Arranging inventories and check-outs
- Liaising with contractors and third parties
- Assisting colleagues during changeover periods
- Supporting the wider team wherever required

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

You'll need:
- Previous experience in a residential lettings contracts, tenancy progression or lettings administration role
- A good working knowledge of current English residential lettings legislation and compliance requirements
- Experience preparing and progressing tenancy agreements
- Experience of referencing, guarantors, deposits and Right to Rent procedures
- Exceptional attention to detail
- Excellent organisation and the ability to manage a large number of applications and deadlines simultaneously
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- Confidence picking up the telephone and speaking to applicants, tenants, parents and guarantors
- The persistence to proactively chase outstanding information and keep applications moving
- Good judgement, discretion and an understanding of the importance of confidentiality and GDPR
- A calm, empathetic manner, particularly when circumstances are sensitive or conversations are difficult
- The ability to work independently while being very much part of a small team

Experience within student accommodation or student lettings would be a considerable advantage.

HOURS:

This is a part-time role of 22.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday, 10 30.

Our busiest period is during the summer changeover and student move-in season, so we're looking for someone who can offer additional hours/flexibility during peak summer periods by prior agreement.

SALARY & BENEFITS:
- £27,000 per annum FTE, pro rata for 22.5 hours per week, depending on experience.
- Company pension scheme
- Private medical insurance
- Employee assistance programme
- Various team events throughout the year

WHY WESTGATE ONE?

Westgate One is Canterbury's newest and (we think) most premium student accommodation offering, based in the heart of our beautiful city.

We aim to offer a level of customer service to our tenants that matches the high standard of our studio properties, so we're looking for the best of the best to join our team.

We're a small team, which means everybody matters. This position has genuine ownership of an important part of the business, and you'll work closely with the onsite team and Operations Director.

We're looking for somebody who takes pride in getting things right, enjoys bringing order to a busy workload and understands that behind every application is a person who needs keeping informed.

If you're highly organised, experienced in lettings compliance and the person who makes sure nothing falls through the cracks, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Clinical Administrator
description: This is a key role within our multidisciplinary team, supporting clinicians by ensuring incoming clinical correspondence is reviewed, processed and accurately recorded. You will identify relevant clinical information, update patient records and ensure correspondence is directed to the right person or team. The role will suit someone who enjoys working with detailed information, follows processes carefully and can use their judgement to identify what can be safely managed and what needs clinical input. You will help reduce unnecessary GP workload while recognising when something is outside your remit and needs to be escalated. Day-to-day work may include reviewing hospital letters, investigation results and other clinical correspondence, extracting and coding relevant information, updating patient records, filing documentation and directing tasks to the appropriate team. You may also support note summarising and other activities that maintain clear, accurate clinical records. Accuracy and patient safety are at the heart of this role. You will need to manage your workload, follow practice and national guidance, and know when to seek advice from a GP, supervisor or manager. By ensuring clinical information is handled accurately, promptly and safely, you will help our clinicians work effectively and support patient care. As a Clinical Administrator, you will help keep the practices clinical and administrative processes running smoothly. Your main duties will include processing incoming clinical correspondence, accurately updating patient records, reviewing and coding clinical information, and ensuring information is directed to the appropriate team member. You will support the processing of hospital and clinic letters, results, safeguarding information and electronic data, as well as summarising new patient records, supporting registrations and managing out-of-area correspondence. Working closely with the clinical team, you will identify and escalate complex or sensitive issues appropriately and support effective communication across the practice. You will also contribute to team meetings and training and help new colleagues learn practice processes. High standards of confidentiality, information governance and accuracy are essential. Job Description Clinical Administrator Job Title: Clinical Administrator Responsible to: Administration Lead, Practice Manager Accountable to: Practice Partnership Hours: Applicants must be available to work within our core operating hours of 08:00-17:30 . We are open to discussing flexibility around shift length and working patterns for the right candidate. Job Summary The Clinical Administrator provides vital support to the multidisciplinary team by managing and processing clinical correspondence and patient records in line with practice and national guidelines. The role focuses on streamlining workflows to reduce unnecessary GP administration, ensuring accurate coding and filing of information, and directing more complex items to the appropriate clinician for review. The post-holder will work as part of the Clinical Administration team, prioritising their workload effectively, maintaining strict confidentiality at all times, and knowing when to escalate matters to supervisors or clinicians. Roles and Responsibilities Ensure all incoming and internal correspondence is stored in patient records. Review and Read Code clinical correspondence before forwarding to clinicians. Process and file hospital letters, reports, emails and other correspondence. Code diagnoses, procedures and investigations accurately. Refer complex or high-risk documents, including safeguarding issues, to the relevant clinician. Summarise new patient records (manual and GP2GP) and process registrations, transfers, and out-of-area notifications. Manage incoming test results, redirect unmatched pathology, and process screening and monitoring results. Process Out of Hours reports and other external communications. Monitor the practice email inbox, flagging urgent queries promptly. Provide administrative cover for other team members when necessary. Open, scan, distribute and file post; manage photocopying and record requests. Assist with training and mentoring of new staff. Maintain a tidy office environment and adhere to a clear desk policy. Teamwork & Communication Work as part of the Clinical Administration Team and the wider practice team. Build effective working relationships with colleagues, patients and external organisations. Communicate clearly and professionally, ensuring confidentiality at all times. Participate in meetings and training, including occasional sessions outside normal hours. General Responsibilities Confidentiality Patients entrust the practice with sensitive information and staff must respect this confidentiality at all times. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues or the practice may only be shared in line with GDPR and practice policies. Health & Safety Follow practice health and safety policies, including infection prevention and control. Use personal security systems as required. Identify risks, manage work safely, and report concerns promptly. Maintain work areas in a safe, hazard-free condition. Equality & Diversity Promote equality of opportunity and respect the rights of patients, carers and colleagues. Act in ways that recognise diversity and ensure fairness, consistent with policy and legislation. Respect privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs at all times. Personal & Professional Development Participate in annual appraisal and performance reviews. Take responsibility for ongoing learning and development. Share skills and knowledge with colleagues and support new staff training. Quality Strive to maintain quality and safety within the practice. Reflect on individual and team activities, suggesting improvements to enhance performance. Manage own time, workload and resources effectively. Communication Communicate effectively with patients, carers, colleagues and external agencies. Adapt communication methods to meet individual needs and ensure understanding.
